\begin{exercise} \end{exercise} 1. ch8:8-10↗ exer:prove-lemma-2-11 ↗ prob:product-metric-curvature Suppose $g = g_1 \oplus g_2$ is a product metric on $M_1 \times M_2$ as in (2.12). (See also Problem 7-6.)

  1. Show that for each point $p_i \in M_i$, the submanifolds $M_1 \times \{ p_2\} $ and $\{ p_1\} \times M_2$ are totally geodesic.

  2. Show that $\sec (\Pi ) = 0$ for every 2-plane $\Pi \subseteq T_{(p_1,p_2)}(M_1 \times M_2)$ spanned by $v_1 \in T_{p_1} M_1$ and $v_2 \in T_{p_2} M_2$.

  3. Show that if $M_1$ and $M_2$ both have nonnegative sectional curvature, then $M_1 \times M_2$ does too; and if $M_1$ and $M_2$ both have nonpositive sectional curvature, then $M_1 \times M_2$ does too.

  4. Now suppose $(M_i, g_i)$ has constant sectional curvature $c_i$ for $i = 1,2$; let $n_i = \dim M_i$. Show that $(M, g)$ is Einstein if and only if $c_1(n_1 - 1) = c_2(n_2 - 1)$; and $(M, g)$ has constant sectional curvature if and only if $n_1 = n_2 = 1$ or $c_1 = c_2 = 0$.

(Used on p. 366.) \end{exercise}
